summary: 1. Key operational findings Oct 17 posted 20,584 BCM against a 24,072.2 BCM target (-14.49%), MTD 469,836 BCM (-7.06% vs target), day 23 of 30 (7 days remaining). 2. Three things to flag: 1. 3. The day's composition set two cycle records at once: waste missed its target by 34.31% (12,896 against 19,637.3 BCM, the largest waste miss of the cycle, surpassing Oct 16's -24.23%) while ore beat its target by 73.37% (7,688 against 4,435.0 BCM, the largest ore surplus of the cycle in absolute BCM), with the MTD ore gap narrowing to -28.14%, its best reading this cycle, even as the MTD total gap widened to -7.06% and broke a three-day narrowing streak (Oct 14 -7.46%, Oct 15 -7.03%, Oct 16 -6.69%). 2. 4. EX-340 opened a new 21-hour hydraulic-leakage breakdown, the heaviest new excavator fault of the day, while EX-247 disappeared entirely from the Daily Availability Final Report's by-exception fault table for the first time this cycle -- read against the Oct 17 HOD meeting's report that EX-247 has entered a major shop repair (PTO leak, wiring harness, hoses, coolant leak, estimated at roughly nine days), this looks like a reclassification to "Suspended" rather than a fresh version of the Oct 14 source conflict, and is treated that way rather than as an open contradiction. 5. DR-125 also opened a new 24-hour undercarriage (track) breakdown, the heaviest drill-rig fault logged this cycle. 3. 6. The 261018-INX-SUM survey workbook landed mid-pass (flagged directly by Peter while this compile was running) and gives the Oct 17 production day's survey reading: 24,114 BCM against 20,584 BCM trucked, +3,530 BCM (+14.64%), narrowing the cumulative survey-versus-trucks gap sharply to -24,389 BCM (-5.48%) from Oct 16's -27,919 BCM (-6.63%) and lifting the required daily recovery rate to 30,934 BCM for Oct 19, the steepest ask of the cycle with one week left in the production month. 7. Fleet availability (Daily Availability Final Report, authoritative over the A&U workbook): excavators 69.05% day / 67.03% MTD, down from Oct 16's 77.98%; trucks 87.23% / 90.53%; drills 83.59% / 87.24%, down sharply from Oct 16's 96.88% on DR-125's new fault; overall 94.17% / 89.09%, core fleet 91.51%. 8. Lost volume: excavators (EX-253 full day, EX-340's new 21 h fault, EX-123's 5 h A/C repair; EX-247 excluded, already carried under the separate nine-day workshop-repair estimate logged Oct 17) 19,100 BCM / 51,570.0 t at planned rates; dump trucks (DT-107, DT-109 full day each, plus DT-108, DT-366, DT-130, DT-243, DT-242 and smaller items) 6,581.2 BCM / 17,769.2 t at today's 61.94 BCM/h fleet rate. 9. Combined gross 25,681.2 BCM / 69,339.2 t. The 261018-SAFETY-BERM email logs an average berm height of 1.43 m, explicitly flagged "below the standard" (average floor level 960.24 m, "good") -- the first below-standard berm reading logged in RAW this cycle, worth a mention at the next HOD meeting. EX-340's breakdown-hour reading disagrees by 2 hours between the Daily Availability Final Report (21 h) and the Client Meeting Report's machinery table (19 h) on an otherwise-agreed fault -- a minor confirmation item for maintenance, not treated as a material source conflict. The new JRAR Q3 performance-review deck that landed today (a differently-named, larger file alongside the already-ingested version) carries a revised cover date (15-Oct, was 12-Oct) but unchanged core figures (-6.1% production vs plan) -- registered, not re-compiled. Articles updated (Last updated 2026-10-17): daily-production-report, fleet-availability-utilization, survey-volume-reconciliation. Key operational findings Oct 16 posted 12,834 BCM against a 12,036.1 BCM target (+6.63%), MTD 449,252 BCM (-6.69% vs target), day 22 of 30 (8 days remaining). Three things to flag: 1. The day's composition is the story, not the total: waste missed by 24.23% (7,440 against 9,818.6 BCM, the cycle's largest waste miss) while ore beat its target by 143.25% (5,394 against 2,217.5 BCM, the cycle's largest ore surplus), with Stage 4 share recovering further to 37.92% -- continuing the gradual return toward Ma'aden's written "Stage 4 first" priority. The general comment "Yesterday was Roster break" explains the smallest absolute daily total this cycle despite the target beat, and accounts for the cluster of 12 h standby entries across the excavator fleet. 2. EX-247's standing low-power/derate fault cleared at 5:30 PM after 12 h down, and for the second day running the Daily Availability Final Report and the Client Meeting Report read the fault identically (12 h, 50.00% avail) -- treating the Oct 14 source conflict as resolved rather than a recurring pattern. 3. DT-109 is logged down the full 24 h for a second day, but today's report calls the fault "Engine Failure" (Engine) where yesterday's called it "No Gear" (Power Train), both dated to the same 15-Oct 11 PM opening with no clearing event between the two reports -- flagged for maintenance to confirm whether this is one incident reclassified or two separate faults. Fleet availability (Daily Availability Final Report, authoritative over the A&U workbook): excavators 77.98% day / 66.91% MTD, up from Oct 15's 75.60%; trucks 93.15% / 90.73%; drills 96.88% / 87.47% -- the cycle's biggest drilling surplus (1,846 m against 1,281.4 m target, +44.06%), after Oct 15's standby-driven miss eased off; overall 97.23% / 88.77%, core fleet 96.17%. Lost volume: excavators (EX-253 full day, EX-247 12 h before clearing, EX-123 1 h) 11,950 BCM / 32,265.0 t at planned rates; dump trucks (DT-107, DT-109, DT-130, DT-246) 3,517.1 BCM / 9,496.1 t at today's 61.17 BCM/h fleet rate. Combined gross 15,467.1 BCM / 41,761.1 t. The Client Meeting Report's own "MTD Actual Survey" cell jumped from 388,268 to 409,572 BCM between the Oct 15 and Oct 16 tabs. By the one-day reporting lag tracked since Oct 9, this is read as the Oct 15 production day's survey figure, even though the standalone 261016-INX-SUM.xlsx workbook has still not landed in RAW on its own. Treated that way, the cumulative survey-versus-trucks gap widens to -26,846 BCM (-6.55% of survey), reversing the narrowing trend running since Oct 13 (Oct 13 -9.69%, Oct 14 -6.14%, now -6.55%). This reading is inferred from the lagged MTD cell, not read from a dated file with its own daily figure and loading-location comment -- flagged in [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] to confirm once the workbook lands. Flag, not resolved (new this pass): two new document families appeared in `Maaden Plans/` -- an ADW Shutdown Preparedness deck/workbook/email set, and an "ADW - 2027 readiness presentation" email in the Q4 Recovery Plans folder. Both registered by name only, not read or compiled. The shutdown-preparedness subject matter overlaps the crusher-shutdown narrative already running in daily-production-report and is worth a dedicated read on a future full compile pass. The A&U, DPR, Drill Meters, Block Info, DPR and A&U docx, Equipment Running Hours, Running Hours Maaden, and Distance Report workbooks gained Oct 16 tabs but were registered by name only, not deep-read (the Client Meeting Report and the Daily Availability Final Report cover the figures compiled this pass). Source: KNOWLEDGE/mining_operations_kb/RAW via the librarian compile protocol.
